newsitem.title: UK: IBCA affirms Storehouse l-term at BBB plus.
newsitem.headline: IBCA affirms Storehouse l-term at BBB plus.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said it affirmed its ratings for Storehouse Plc.
"The long-term rating remains BBB plus and the short-term is A2," IBCA said.
"Progress in the last few years has been good as resources have been focussed on building the strength of the core Bhs and Mothercare businesses," IBCA said in a statement.

"Improved margins underline the reduced emphasis on price discounting and the benefits of enhanced operational efficiency, examples of which include slimming of the supplier base and integration of the Bhs and Mothercare distribution functions at a single depot," IBCA said.

"Organic store chain expansion and the store refurbishment and extension programme are ongoing, whilst the post FYE96 purchase of Childrens World from Boots added 56 specialist out-of-town stores to be incorporated into the Mothercare chain," IBCA said.

"The cost of the acquisition used up the group's YE net cash resources of 74 million stg and together with capital spending of c. 110 million stg in FY97, will likely result in a small net cash outflow in the current year," IBCA said.
"Nonetheless, the financial structure (net gearing of only 8 percent at H1FY97) remains prudent and supports the current ratings," IBCA said.

"Storehouse expects to see further growth in sales in FY97, both in the UK and from a continued rise in the contribution from overseas franchise sales which rose by 38 percent during H1FY97," IBCA said.
